paper_metadata.title: Effect of Nb addition on glass-forming ability, strength, and hardness of Fe–B–Zr amorphous alloys

evidence.quote: Supercooled liquid region ( DTx), tensile fracture strength ( sf), and Vickers hardness (Hv) of Fe–B–Zr–Nb amorphous alloys were measured.
Multicomponent alloys with composition Fe 70B20Zr102xNbx (x 5 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10) were examined in this study
Figure 1 shows the DSC curves of the melt-spun Fe70B20Zr102xNbx (x 5 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10) amorphous alloys (hereafter referred to as Nb0, Nb2, Nb4, Nb6, Nb8, and Nb10, respectively).

other.charge: pure Fe, Zr, Nb metals and pure B crystal; purity 99.5-99.9%

evidence.quote: Master ingots were prepared by arc melting a mixture of pure Fe, Zr, and Nb metals and pure B crystal in a water-cooled copper boat under an argon atmosphere.
Rapidly solidified ribbons with a cross section of 0.015 3 1.0 mm2 were prepared by single-roller melt-spinning the master ingots in an argon atmosphere.

evidence.quote: the topological and chemical short-range orderings are enhanced, leading to the formation of a highly dense random packed structure, which results in high thermal stability of the supercooled liquid against crystallization as well as high resistance to mechanical failure.

The weaker bonding nature of the Nb-contained pairs, as compared with the Zr-contained pairs, seems to result in the decrease in DT x for the alloys containing more than 4 at% Nb (Nb6, Nb8, Nb10 alloys).

The addition of appropriate amount (2– 4 at%) of Nb to the Fe–B–Zr system leads to the increase of mechanical strength due to the satisfaction of the three empirical rules for achievement of high GFA metallic glass and increase of packing density of the amorphous phases.
Therefore, both GFA and mechanical strength increase with increasing packing density from ternary system to quaternary system with appropriate amount of Nb.
the tensile fracture strength and Vickers hardness values of the alloys can be ranked in the same order as theDT x values, that is, Nb4 . Nb2 . Nb0 . Nb6 . Nb8 . Nb10.
